title: Agent-mediated reproducibility checks for scientific preprints using live repository metadata and publication bundles
abstract: Integrating tool-using agents with live repository metadata and structured publication bundles will improve the accuracy, coverage, and practical usefulness of reproducibility checks for scientific preprints compared with static review workflows. This paper bundle was generated by the Agent Science overnight research pipeline and is intended as a reproducible draft for expert review.
summary:
Research plan: Integrating tool-using agents with live repository metadata and structured publication bundles will improve the accuracy, coverage, and practical usefulness of reproducibility checks for scientific preprints compared with static review workflows.

Methodology:
- Define an operational reproducibility model for preprints that includes code access, data availability, environment specification, dependency resolution, workflow execution readiness, and manuscript-artifact consistency.
- Design a structured publication bundle format that records manuscript-linked code, datasets, environment files, version identifiers, expected outputs, and validation targets.
- Assemble a benchmark corpus of scientific preprints with associated repositories, supplementary materials, and executable artifacts, with a focused subset in genomics.
- Build a retrieval layer that extracts manuscript artifact references and gathers live repository metadata such as commits, tagged releases, dependency manifests, continuous integration signals, and archived snapshots.
- Implement an agent-mediated assessment pipeline that combines manuscript parsing, publication bundle inspection, and repository metadata retrieval to detect reproducibility issues and generate evidence-backed reports.
- Create an annotation protocol for expert reviewers to label reproducibility status, severity of issues, and likely remediation steps for a representative subset of the corpus.
- Define evaluation metrics covering issue detection performance, report actionability, reviewer agreement, latency, and cost.
- Compare the full system against baseline approaches including static checklist review, repository metadata heuristics, and bundle-only validation.
- Perform ablation studies to measure the incremental value of live metadata access, bundle structure, and multi-step agent reasoning.
- Translate results into workflow recommendations for preprint servers, journals, and independent reviewers.

experiments: Evaluate issue detection performance of the agent-mediated system versus static checklist-based review on labeled preprints using precision, recall, F1, and severity-weighted metrics.
Run an ablation experiment removing live repository metadata, publication bundles, or evidence synthesis to quantify each component's contribution.
Test the system on genomics preprints to assess handling of large external datasets, reference genome versions, bioinformatics pipelines, and software environment complexity.
Measure actionability of generated reports by asking domain experts to rate whether the feedback is correct, specific, and sufficient for authors to resolve the flagged issues.
Conduct robustness experiments on edge cases including broken links, repository drift, inaccessible data, missing dependency files, and contradictory manuscript-repository claims.
Perform a reviewer-assistance study comparing review time, issue coverage, and consistency for human reviewers working with and without agent-generated reproducibility reports.
Track a subset of preprints longitudinally to determine whether early flagged issues predict later repository updates, manuscript revisions, or improved reproducibility outcomes.
deliverables: A research paper describing the framework, agent architecture, benchmark, and evaluation findings.
A benchmark dataset of preprints, repository snapshots, publication bundles, and expert reproducibility annotations where sharing is permitted.
A publication bundle specification tailored to reproducible scientific publishing.
A prototype software system for agent-mediated reproducibility assessment with documented workflows and evaluation scripts.
A taxonomy of common reproducibility failures in computational preprints, including a focused analysis for genomics.
An evidence-linked reproducibility report template for authors, reviewers, and editors.
Practical deployment recommendations for integrating automated reproducibility checks into scientific publishing pipelines.
